text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Health Ministry will promote government doctors faster and raise their allowances in a move to stem brain drain to private sector.
- President Suharto of Indonesia calls on conglomerates to honour their commitments to help the needy.
- Jurong Town Corp undergoes major revamp to make itself more customer focused in order to draw more foreign investments in the face of mounting competition.
- Housing Board has incurred an overall operating deficit of Singapore $1.44 billion from its housing activities for the year ended March 1996.
- New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd sells its entire 20.17 per cent stake in Commerce-Asset Holding Bhd to FCW Holdings Bhd for M$969 million.

- Hong Leong group is discussing with several hotel groups, including the Regent, Fairmont and Hilton, a possible merger with its Hongkong-listed CDL Hotels International and to establish a chain of luxury hotels.
- Taiwanese banks and brokers snap up a quarter of Asia Pulp & Paper's US$500 million latest debt issue, but some of their purchases have come under scrutiny of Taiwan's finanical regulators.
- Crosby securities in its latest economy update says that pessimistic reports on Thailand are overblown.

- US-based cellular infrastructure company Celcore Inc has sold a 10-percent equity stake to Thailand's listed United Communication Industry Public Co Ltd in an effort to jump-start its expansion in Asia.
